problem:
The following table gives the values of functions $f(x)$ and ${f}^{′}(x)$ at some points. Find $({f}^{-1})^{′}(5).$

| **$x$** | $f(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $5$ | $-6$ |
| $3$ | $-3$ | $5$ |
worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse is

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Substituting $x=5,$ we have

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(5)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(5))}.
$$

From the table, we obtain ${f}^{-1}(5)=1$ and ${f}^{′}(1)=-6.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(5) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(5))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-6)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
